title: APEX-Accounting
abstract: We introduce APEX-Accounting, a benchmark built by Mercor in partnership with Ramp, to assess whether frontier models can do the real work of accountants. Tasks include reconciling accounts, accruing expenses, posting transactions, and producing reports. The private eval set comprises 160 tasks, split across 10 worlds. Each world contains an accounting system, as well as spreadsheets, PDFs, and other files. Every task was authored and solved by experts in accounting and bookkeeping, who also wrote grading rubrics. Across nine frontier models, Claude-Fable-5 (Max) leads with 56.4% Mean Criteria@3, ahead of Muse-Spark-1.1 (xHigh) at 52.6%. No model scores more than 2.6% Pass^8 (GPT-5.6-Sol (Max+Pro)) and the highest Pass@8 is 21.5% (Muse-Spark-1.1 (xHigh)). We experiment with increasing the token budget from $1 to $50 and observe an instance of Simpson's paradox: scores increase as the token budget increases but within a given budget-constrained harness, scores are lower on tasks where the model spends more tokens. As APEX-Accounting is a closed benchmark, leaderboard evals can be run for any frontier model on request.

significance.justification: The paper introduces a benchmark for evaluating frontier models on real accounting tasks, providing measurable performance data that can inform builders' decisions about model selection for financial applications.

novelty.justification: The benchmark applies established evaluation methodologies to the specific domain of accounting, creating a clear delta from prior general-purpose benchmarks but within a well-trodden line of research.

reproducibility.justification: The paper states APEX-Accounting is a closed benchmark with leaderboard evals available on request, but the method is only partially specified and reproduction would require significant guesswork without access to the private dataset.

clarity.justification: The paper is solidly written, clearly presenting the benchmark's construction, tasks, and results including an interesting observation of Simpson's paradox in token budget experiments.

topical_fit.justification: The paper directly evaluates frontier LLMs on practical tasks, clearly in scope for builders who need to understand model capabilities for real-world applications like accounting.
